title: Nodal curves characterized by a local complete intersection and unramified Jacobian subscheme
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be a scheme locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], equidimensional of dimension $1$ [def-weil-pure-dimension]. Let $Z=\operatorname{Sing}(C/k)$ be its first-Fitting singular subscheme [def-trf-first-fitting-singular-subscheme]. The following are equivalent: (1) every closed point of $C$ is either smooth over $k$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] or a node; here a closed point $x$ [def-weil-closed-points] is a node if some point $\bar x$ of the base change $C_{\bar k}$ [def-pc-base-change] over $x$, for an algebraic closure $\bar k$ of $k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure], has completed local ring (the $\mathfrak m_{\bar x}$-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] of $\mathcal O_{C_{\bar k},\bar x}$) isomorphic to $\bar k[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]; (2) $C$ is a local complete intersection over $k$ and $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is unramified [def-weil-unramified-morphism]. In (2), local complete intersection means that $C$ has an affine open cover by spectra of finitely generated $k$-algebras which are local complete intersections as defined in [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field].

source.place: Tag 0C4E (lemma-nodal-lci), with definition-nodal and Tag 0C4D (lemma-nodal) for the node condition

proof.text: Let $Z$ be the first-Fitting singular subscheme. To apply [lem-trf-dth-fitting-smooth-locus] with relative dimension $d=1$, check its hypotheses: $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is flat because every $k$-module is flat, and it is locally of finite presentation by [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth] since $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally Noetherian and the given morphism is locally of finite type. Every nonempty geometric fibre, i.e. $C_\Omega=C\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ for an algebraically closed extension $\Omega$ of $k$, is equidimensional of dimension $1$ by [lem-trf-flat-dense-generic-fibre-pure-dimension] with $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $d=1$: $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is integral with generic point $\eta$ its only point, $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is flat and locally of finite type, and the generic fibre $C_\eta=C\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}k=C$ is dense in $C$ with all irreducible components of dimension $1$. The Fitting lemma therefore identifies $|Z|$ with the complement of the smooth locus. Finally, if $z\in Z$, [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space] gives a closed point $x$ in the closure of $\{z\}$; since $Z$ is closed, $x\in Z$. We do not assume that the original point $z$ is closed.

source.place: Tag 0C3K and curves Tag 0C4E, first paragraph of the proof

proof.text: Assume (1). Let $z\in Z$. By step 1 choose a closed specialization $x$ of $z$ lying in $Z$. Condition (1) makes $x$ nodal, so [lem-trf-nodal-point-local-criterion] gives an affine local-complete-intersection neighbourhood of $x$, a finite separable residue extension $\kappa(x)/k$, and $\mathcal O_{Z,x}=\kappa(x)$. The latter equality makes the local ring of $Z$ at $x$ a field; since $z$ specializes to $x$, the corresponding inclusion of primes in $\mathcal O_{Z,x}$ forces $z=x$. Thus every point of $Z$ is closed and satisfies the pointwise nodal criterion. At every point outside $Z$, step 1 gives smoothness, and smoothness gives a local complete-intersection neighbourhood by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-over-field-local-complete-intersection] (the smooth ring maps on affine charts are locally complete intersections). These affine neighbourhoods give the required local-complete-intersection cover of $C$. The morphism $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally of finite type, since on an affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $C$ with $A$ a finitely generated $k$-algebra $Z$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(A/\operatorname{Fit}_1)$ and a quotient of a finitely generated algebra is finitely generated. The closedness, the local equalities and the finite separability at all points of $Z$, together with [lem-trf-unramified-over-field-local-criterion] applied to $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, show that $Z$ is unramified.

source.place: Tag 0C4E (lemma-nodal-lci), proof of (1) implies (2), using Tags 02G7 and 0C4D

proof.text: Assume (2). Apply [lem-trf-unramified-over-field-local-criterion] to $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Every point $x\in Z$ is closed, has local ring equal to its residue field, and has finite separable residue extension over $k$. Since $C$ is a local complete intersection, the affine cover in (2) supplies an affine local-complete-intersection neighbourhood of each such $x$; the converse direction of [lem-trf-nodal-point-local-criterion] therefore shows that every point of $Z$ is a node. By step 1, every point outside $Z$ is smooth. Hence all closed points are smooth or nodes, proving (1).

split_report.summary: Repaired the returned split against Curves Tags 0C4E, 0C4D and 0C4C. Step 1 now checks flatness, local finite presentation, and geometric equidimensionality before applying the Fitting smooth-locus lemma, and uses the existing Jacobson node to specialize each singular point to a closed point without falsely declaring all singular points closed. Step 2 then proves that the field stalk at that closed specialization forces the original singular point to equal it, cites the existing smooth-over-a-field local-complete-intersection node, and removes the stale unramified tool-use entry. The pointwise node now defines a node inline, states an affine local-complete-intersection neighbourhood rather than an ill-typed local-ring property, and includes all definition dependencies required by its statement. Maintainer reader fix (2026-10-18): step 1 now takes the geometric equidimensionality from the existing same-unit node lem-trf-flat-dense-generic-fibre-pure-dimension (base Spec k), so the new geometric-equidimensionality node of this delivery is dropped; the statements cite def-weil-pure-dimension for equidimensionality and the completion, power-series, closed-point, base-change and algebraic-closure definitions; step 2 records finiteness of the residue fields and local finite type of Z.
split_report.blueprint: The three steps realize the 0C4E proof paragraphs: first the smooth-locus/Fitting reduction and specialization to closed singular points, then (1) implies (2) using the 0C4D pointwise criterion and smooth-to-lci fact, and finally (2) implies (1).

lean.statement: theorem nodal_curve_lci_criterion (k : Type u) [Field k] (C : Scheme.{u}) (f : C ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (hC : C.IsPureDimension 1) : (∀ x : C, x ∈ closedPoints C → (x ∈ (f.smoothLocus : Set C) ∨ ∃ xbar : (pullback (C := Scheme.{u}) f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (AlgebraicClosure k))))), pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (AlgebraicClosure k)))) xbar = x ∧ Nonempty (AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal ((pullback (C := Scheme.{u}) f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (AlgebraicClosure k))))).presheaf.stalk xbar)) ((pullback (C := Scheme.{u}) f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (AlgebraicClosure k))))).presheaf.stalk xbar) ≃+* (MvPowerSeries (Fin 2) (AlgebraicClosure k) ⧸ Ideal.span {(MvPowerSeries.X 0 : MvPowerSeries (Fin 2) (AlgebraicClosure k)) * (MvPowerSeries.X 1 : MvPowerSeries (Fin 2) (AlgebraicClosure k))})))) ↔ ((∀ x : C, ∃ U : C.affineOpens, x ∈ U.1 ∧ ∃ (ft : @Algebra.FiniteType k Γ(C, U.1) _ _ ((f.appLE ⊤ U.1 (by simp)).hom.comp (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv.hom).toAlgebra), @Algebra.IsLocalCompleteIntersection k Γ(C, U.1) _ _ ((f.appLE ⊤ U.1 (by simp)).hom.comp (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv.hom).toAlgebra ft) ∧ (LocallyOfFiniteType (Scheme.firstFittingSingularSubscheme f ≫ f) ∧ IsOpenImmersion (pullback.diagonal (Scheme.firstFittingSingularSubscheme f ≫ f))))
